answer.rationale: A release went out 2 hours ago and p99 write-path latency has been climbing for 90 minutes—roughly 30 minutes after the deploy. The timing correlation strongly suggests the new build is the proximate cause. Memory_b1 (day 18) records that rolling back a release cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact, and the prior build was stable. Settling on rollback directly removes the suspected root cause while the prior known-good build handles the peak settlement write load, preserving availability and writes. Regional failover, circuit breakers, and read-replica routing address different failure modes (latency from region-level issues, partner outages, and read-heavy dashboards respectively) and would not remove the regression. Adding capacity treats the symptom without fixing the cause. Rolling back is the fastest, most targeted intervention to maximize sustained availability without losing customer writes.
